context: Wilde to Frank Harris, [circa 26 July 1899], Hotel de l'Ecu, Chenneviers-sur-Marne. Asking for £15 and hiding from a hotel keeper he owes. The postscript is the whole point of the letter: at this address he is using his own name, not Melmoth, and he asks Harris to do the same.
quote:
Hotel de l’Écu, Chenneviers-sur-Marne, Seine et Oise.

My dear Frank — I don’t know if you have any money going — or if the Transvaal belongs to you now or not — I am in a great mess over things — and if you have £15 that you would like to throw to the poets, do send me a cheque for it. I am dreadfully worried by hotel-patrons — only one — but a tiger from the Hotel Marsollier — coming down and making life horrible — and I have no money —

Ever Oscar

Please write to me under _my real_ name here —

Oscar Wilde
original_provenance: Read at HRC 2676, images 50-51 - one folded sheet of squared paper, three sides used: 50 is side 1, 51 the opening of sides 2 and 3, the postscript standing alone on side 3. Emphasis: one underline, '_my real_' in the postscript, running across the line break - the stroke is under 'my' at the end of one line and under 'real' at the head of the next, so it is a single mark on the phrase and not a line-break artefact, the same shape as '_rien compris_' at pp. 1124-1125. The volume italicises it. Fifth confirmed case of a printed italic on ordinary English recording a real mark. It is also the most pointed mark in the folder. He signs the letter 'Oscar' and then signs the postscript 'Oscar Wilde' in full, and the underline falls on the words asking to be written to under his own name. This is the one letter of the five in this cluster with no Sebastian Melmoth heading, which is what the postscript is about. Null: 'patrons' is not underlined; the volume's italic there is its French convention. Address: he writes 'Seine et Oise', which the volume omits from the heading. Punctuation: his dashes carry the letter almost entirely; the volume converts them to full stops and commas.
